title: every_emitted_remedy_names_something_this_build_can_do asserts a verb is wired, never that following the remedy changes the situation
body:
**A TEST WHOSE NAME CLAIMS MORE THAN ITS BODY CHECKS.** `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/remedies_are_reachable.rs`, test `every_emitted_remedy_names_something_this_build_can_do`.

It asserts `wiredness(&fx, &r) == Wired::No` -- ie that the verb a remedy names is WIRED. **It never asks whether FOLLOWING the remedy changes the situation the remedy was emitted for.**

## Why the distinction is not academic

A remedy is a promise to an operator: *do this and your problem goes away.* A wired verb is a necessary condition for that promise and nowhere near a sufficient one. **The failure mode is an operator doing exactly what they were told and nothing changing** -- and `0241`'s sibling class showed this is not hypothetical: `browsed()` told an operator to run `intent daemon start` while a daemon was already running. The remedy named a wired verb. The test passed. The advice was useless.

**It passed on `--browser`'s false remedy and it passes on the fix**, which is the sharpest statement of the gap: the test cannot distinguish the broken state from the repaired one, so it was never evidence about either.

## Measured 2026-09-04

- **186 remedy emissions.**
- **24 name a verb whose precondition may ALREADY BE SATISFIED** -- ie following the remedy is a no-op for a caller already in that state.

## The open question, stated as unmeasured

**Does anything, anywhere, drive a remedy and then re-check the original error?** Not measured. The obvious grep does not answer it -- `grep -rc remedy native/rust/crates/intent-cli/src/*.rs` lists files MENTIONING the word, which is a population of files and not a population of behaviours. **An instrument for this needs the emitted remedy and the re-drive to be the same subject**, and no existing test has that shape.

## What this is NOT

Not a claim that the 24 are defects. A remedy whose precondition is already satisfied may still be the right thing to print. **The defect is that nothing can tell the two apart**, which is the same class as a control that cannot come out the other way.

Filed by vc. The measurement is vc's; the open question is unassigned at filing.
## The open question is ANSWERED (ic, 2026-09-04). Nothing does -- and both halves already exist.

**NOTHING, ANYWHERE, DRIVES A REMEDY AND RE-CHECKS THE ORIGINAL ERROR.** Measured
across three populations, no harness built.

| population | size | read a remedy | drive one |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rust test functions | 2151 | 55 | 0 |
| bats tests | 1491 | 2 | 0 |
| non-test Rust sites | -- | 37 | 0 |

The single Rust candidate was examined and is a FALSE POSITIVE:
`doctor_advisory_summary.rs::the_summary_counts_advisories_apart_and_exits_zero_on_them_alone`
asserts a remedy is DISPLAYED (`remedy: nothing is owed now`) and never follows
one. It is itself an instance of the 24 -- a remedy whose precondition is
satisfied by construction. All 37 non-test sites are bare `e.remedy()`
expressions feeding a renderer; none acts.

### The sharper finding: the halves exist, in the same files, and nothing joins them

This is not a capability the estate lacks. **It is a seam nothing owns.**

`intent browse st ST0001` with no daemon refuses and the refusal names
`intent daemon start`. `edit_and_browse_reach_one_model.rs` asserts that
refusal AND, in a different test in the SAME FILE, stands up a `RealDaemon`
and drives the same verb to success. Both halves are already written. Nothing
connects them, so **the remedy text could be replaced with nonsense and every
test in that file stays green.** Same shape in `graphql_escape_hatch.rs` and
`routing_is_opt_in.rs`.

That is why `every_emitted_remedy_names_something_this_build_can_do` reads as
sufficient and is not: it checks the remedy names a wired verb, and the
separate tests check the verb works. **Neither checks that THIS remedy
resolves THIS error**, and no third test does either.

### What the instrument's population is, and what it deliberately excludes

The population is **subjects that READ an emitted remedy** -- vc's "the
emitted remedy and the re-drive must be ONE SUBJECT". A test that plants a
failure, hard-codes the fix and re-checks WITHOUT referencing the remedy is
out of population **on purpose**: it validates the mechanism, not the promise,
and would stay green if the remedy said something else entirely. Those tests
do exist; they are the unjoined halves above.

### How the instrument was controlled, because a zero is the easiest number to get wrong

- **Positive control, both directions.** A synthetic test that reads a remedy
  then re-drives was planted OUTSIDE the repository and the detector reported
  `DRIVES`; a plain remedy-reader beside it reported `reads only`. The
  detector can come out the other way, so the zero is a measurement.
- **Comments stripped before scanning**, and this was load-bearing rather than
  tidy: **14 of the 16 remedy mentions in `.bats` are PROSE in comments.**
  Counting them would have reported 16 readers where there are 2, and the same
  strip is why the Rust count is 55 rather than higher.
- **The execution vocabulary was DERIVED, not guessed** -- `Command::new` with
  `CARGO_BIN_EXE_intent` is the dominant form (89 sites). A guessed pattern is
  how a surface gets bounded by one of two argument grammars.
- **The bats shortfall was chased rather than accepted**: 11 files mention a
  remedy but only 2 in-test lines do, and the difference is fully accounted
  for by comments (14) with 0 outside a test block.

**NO HARNESS WAS BUILT**, per the constraint on this issue. Whether one should
exist -- and it would have to make the emitted remedy and the re-drive one
subject -- is a scope call and is not taken here.
